scope: Source-backed reconstruction of Artemis II manual piloting, proximity-operations planning, as-flown manual-control demonstrations, crew-versus-automated control authority, and public control-mode evidence while preserving strict separation between planned sequences and as-flown execution and without reconstructing unavailable controller histories, control laws, thruster-allocation logic, or individual thruster firings.

sources.title: Artemis II SLS Reference Guide
claims_used: The public reference guide provides a 17-step Artemis II proximity-operations demonstration sequence.
The sequence includes HQ 10 m evaluation number 1 and HQ 15 m evaluation number 2.
The sequence ends with auxiliary departure and a long-range flight test objective.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Update: Apogee Raise Burn Complete, Crew Looks Ahead to Proximity Operations
claims_used: The proximity-operations demonstration was planned for approximately 70 minutes.
Orion would automatically turn to face the ICPS before manual close-range operations.
At approximately 300 feet Orion would stop relative motion and the crew would take control.
The crew would use translational and rotational hand controllers and displays.
At about 30 feet Orion would stop for fine handling-quality evaluation.
Very close maneuvers would use European Service Module reaction-control-system thrusters.
An automated departure burn would conclude the demonstration.
The docking camera would gather positioning measurements during departure for future rendezvous-navigation knowledge.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Update: Proximity Operations Complete, Perigee Raise Burn Up Next
claims_used: The proximity-operations demonstration was successfully completed.
The activity lasted approximately 70 minutes.
The crew performed a series of controlled approach and retreat maneuvers relative to the detached ICPS.
The demonstration used onboard navigation sensors and reaction-control thrusters.
Orion executed an automated departure burn at the conclusion of the demonstration.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 4: Crew Completes Manual Piloting Demonstration
claims_used: Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen took turns controlling Orion.
The manual piloting demonstration began at 9:09 p.m. EDT.
The demonstration lasted 41 minutes.
The crew tested six-degrees-of-freedom and three-degrees-of-freedom thruster modes.

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 8: Crew Conducts Key Tests on Return to Earth
claims_used: A manual piloting demonstration had been planned for approximately 10:55 p.m. EDT.
The planned activity included centering a designated target.
The planned activity included guiding Orion to a tail-to-Sun attitude.
Flight controllers elected to forgo the 10:55 p.m. EDT manual piloting demonstration.

sources.title: NASA's Artemis II Moon Mission Daily Agenda
claims_used: The Flight Day 8 manual-piloting plan included centering a target, moving Orion to a tail-to-Sun attitude, and comparing six-degree-of-freedom and three-degree-of-freedom attitude-control modes.

time_policy.rule: NASA explicitly reported the relevant Flight Day 4 and Flight Day 8 local times as EDT. MissionLab therefore converts those source timestamps using the fixed reported UTC-04:00 offset rather than adding an IANA tzdata dependency.
time_policy.derived_met_rule: Mission elapsed time is derived from the configured Artemis II launch epoch. Derived values inherit the public timestamp precision of their source anchors.

geometry_context.interpretation: The mission update and SLS reference guide provide related but differently expressed planned geometry. MissionLab preserves each source statement and does not force exact equivalence between the approximately 30-foot narrative stop and either reference-guide evaluation step.

guardrails: The 17-step proximity-operations sequence is a premission plan and is not an as-flown step-by-step event log.
Planned proximity range values are not measured as-flown Artemis II relative-range history.
The approximately 70-minute as-flown duration does not establish exact proximity-operations start or stop timestamps.
A manual-control mode does not mean that the hand controller directly switches individual thrusters.
A crew controller command is not an individual thruster-firing history.
Reported RCS use does not establish the exact thruster-allocation sequence.
The six-degrees-of-freedom mode label does not disclose the six-DOF control algorithm.
The three-degrees-of-freedom mode label does not disclose the three-DOF control algorithm.
Successful completion of proximity operations does not prove that every premission reference-guide step executed exactly as planned.
The approximately 300-foot and about 30-foot planning descriptions are not confirmed as-flown range measurements.
The reference-guide 10 m and 15 m handling-quality evaluation labels are planning geometry and are not promoted to as-flown range measurements.
The narrative approximately 30-foot stop is not silently forced to be identical to either the 10 m or 15 m reference-guide evaluation.
The confirmed automated departure does not establish the exact manual-to-automatic transition time.
The Flight Day 8 planned manual demonstration was foregone and must not be represented as executed.
The Flight Day 8 planned timestamp is not an executed GNC event timestamp.
The docking-camera measurement context is not promoted to a confirmed closed-loop navigation input without explicit evidence.
